citations.review_text:
Initially I wrote a novel on why I dislike ICARUS,  so I'll format it down to something smaller:

1. I have played for 69 minutes. out of that I spent 40 minutes trying to get the game to run.

2. I've had 3 crashes during the bonkers long boot up, 1 crash mid game on the lowest settings, and whooping 7 
    crashes trying to load into a world!

3. This game does NOT lie with it's minimum specs. Between Windows 10, Steam and ICARUS, I constantly peaked 
    at 95% ram usage with 16 gigabytes. Icarus uses up 4gb just on it's loading screen alone.

4. Performance - The game struggled to maintain 120 fps on a overclocked RTX 2060,  which  I wouldn't  blame 
    due to its smaller sized 6GB of VRAM, if that wasn't on Minimum settings!

5. The graphics are actually bad, on anything below medium, and medium does require the Elusive rtx 3060Ti or 
    3070 to just be playable. Melting my computer to see the game on high settings, yeah the graphics are okay. 
    For the performance you get, you should honestly question what eats up all the resources. The optimization all 
    around is bad, I've seen blender scenes run better quality and performance wise.

6. As for the gameplay, I did not see much, and I won't see much. For the 30 minutes I played, the most eye 
    catching thing was rocks deforming when you hit them, that's it, not even in a good way. It was okay fun for 30 
    minutes, then I lost interest.

7. The UI is, as most people say, atrocious. It is very confusing, over bloated and over complicated. It feels over 
    stimulating, item portraits relatively blend together creating confusion of mousing over each one to locate 
    which one is the correct one to make.

As a lover of survival games, this feels like someone's take on 7 days to die x Ark survival Evolved with focus on realistic wilderness over poorly optimized dinosaurs and zombies. I cannot recommend this game from the perspective of how badly it ran, it was a stream of constant out of memory iss…

Clunky is honestly the only word I can think of to describe the game. Everything feels clunky. Moving through menus, crafting, inventory management, its clunky. Progression immediately feels bad, hopefully you look at your tech tree a bit and realize soon that you need to rush to unlock the ability to make oxygen. Also, why do you need oxygen on a planet that has normal wolves and bears? Air seems fine enough for them. Huge tech/ability tree, unlock screens and currencies overwhelm you with useless information before you even start playing.

I would have gone more in depth but the game is honestly so mediocre it isnt even worth the time.

Im sure this game is good when it works, but the many people online trying to trouble shoot issues is quite large.
For me the game does not seem to be able to render its own graphics properly, no matter on what settings.

There are also no scaling options for text or UI, and the default is made without taking into account that people play on different resolutions and screen sizes. The developers have a website where UI and text scaling is asked for extensively and the status is always ''under consideration''. So after 4,5 years they wont add basic settings like this anymore, that chance is long gone.

Try it during a free weekend to see if its playable at all, since you might need the 2+ hours just to troubleshoot and get it to work.
There are no developers active on the forums, so if it does not work it wont get fixed.

citations.review_text: looks great and has all the things to be a good game, except a story and a purpose for playing. missions suck, and everything is locked behind DLC.

Icarus feels like a survival experience constantly at war with its own mechanics. Instead of a meaningful journey, progression turns into a relentless, action-based grind where you frenetically engage in every minor activity just to level up. This task-heavy loop completely undermines the sense of real danger, stripping the environment of any actual threat. Even the severe storms fail to pose a genuine challenge, reducing weather survival to a tedious chore of constantly repairing damaged structures.

Consequently, navigating its massive, desolate landscapes quickly becomes boring and empty, making exploration feel deeply unrewarding. The game's structure is equally disjointed: the absence of a coherent storyline leaves you with sporadic, random quests that often disrupt balancing by handing out overpowered gear, like free rifles, far too early. To top it off, combat feels stiff with wooden enemy AI, and performance remains poorly optimized, suffering from unstable framerates even on a high-end RTX 5070. 

What could have been an immersive wilderness survival game ends up feeling like an uninspired, clunky chore.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires a heavy time investment and features a relentless grind.

citations.review_text:
After a long weekend playing solo, this gets a qualified thumbs up from me. There's a lot to like, but it demands a serious time investment and a tolerance for its particular brand of tedium.

The early game is brutally punishing, but there's a satisfying payoff as you build your character, unlock better equipment and learn the systems. I suspect it takes hundreds of hours to really master everything thrown at you.

The grind is relentless. You can become a slave to your own survival, constantly chopping, mining, smelting, cooking, farming and repairing. There's satisfaction in that loop, but it crowds out the genuinely beautiful open world I *want* to explore. Nearly 20 hours in, I still feel far from settled in.

The storms are my biggest complaint. Initially threatening and interesting, they're so frequent that they quickly become interruptions rather than events. More broadly, the game seems determined to knock you down a notch at every turn, constantly fighting your success rather than letting you enjoy it for a while.

Combat becomes fairly trivial a few tiers in, and wildlife is so abundant that it becomes more nuisance than threat. Simply defending your base leaves you with piles of meat, fur, leather and bone you have no practical use for.

There's clearly a lot I haven't seen, but I'm already questioning how much of it I want to. I've enjoyed my time here, but the grind and constant interruptions are crowding out the parts I find most compelling.

After 115 hours, I can honestly say ICARUS is highly addictive if you enjoy survival crafting games with real progression and consequences.

It is a PvE survival game where you gather resources, craft tools and gear, build bases, hunt, explore dangerous biomes, and manage oxygen, water, food, weather, injuries, and wildlife. You start out with sticks and stones, and before long you’re building outposts, running power, farming, using mounts, and unlocking much better technology.

The gameplay loop gets me every time. I’ll log on planning to gather a few materials or finish one upgrade, and suddenly I’ve lost hours expanding a base, chasing a resource I need, or wandering into a new area.

The game can be brutal, especially early on. A lightning storm burned down my very first wooden shelter just minutes after I finished it. Naturally, I learned about the fire whacker afterward. That pretty much sums up the ICARUS experience sometimes. It can be punishing, but it makes the wins feel earned.

It can be grindy, and it does not hold your hand. Weather, predators, injuries, and bad planning can ruin your day fast. But if you like games like Valheim, ARK, or other PvE base-building survival games, there is a lot to enjoy here.

My biggest complaint is performance. Even on a 4080 Super, I still get stutters and occasional frame drops that feel like they should not be happening. It is not enough to make me quit, but it gets frustrating during storms, fights, or around bigger bases.

Still, 115 hours says a lot. It has rough edges, but the survival, crafting, exploration, and progression loop is seriously addictive. If this is your kind of game, you’ll probably lose way more time to it than you planned.

My more than 2,000 hours of playtime should speak for itself: this truly is a fantastic game.

I may not be young anymore—I’m 46—but whenever I have some free time and want to relax, I still launch the game and play. I always manage to come up with another project or goal to work toward, and the best thing is that there is always something new to discover or do.

There is one important issue I would like to mention. I am only bringing it up now because I think I have finally come up with a reasonable solution.

The game is optimized the way it is, and as a programmer myself, I completely understand that improving performance can be an extremely difficult task. However, in some of my long-running saves—where I have essentially built my dream city—the game becomes increasingly difficult to play whenever a storm arrives.

Yes, the storms are the main issue.

7.9/10 could be improved if added fast travel and improved biome of mountain and desert

Awesome game for a open world survival craft. I love the mount and taming system that also has a variety of plants you can grow. Missions keep the game pretty refreshing with constant updates to improve the functions, bugs and items. The DLC's are all pretty great at increasing the further playabillty for mid to late levels with new maps, hunts, and bosses but at a slightly (in my opinion) high cost. 

 The maps are vast, full of life with a lot of stuff to build and do, biomes are large but desert and mountain biomes can be pretty barren and underwhelming at times. I understand the realism of such biomes but it does make for poor gameplay as I just feel like its a task running through to get to my objective, which does bring me to my last gripe with Icarus, Fast travel. The maps are huge and sometimes take over 10 min to travel across with zero fast travel. If you play on open world and do a round trip, it can take 20 min just in traveling there not including the mission itself or the travel within the mission. Very confusing since there's already a perfect mechanic for it using the pods you came to the planet in and could leave in. I hope they add that in a later update. 

All in all I give it a solid 7.9/10

Icarus is a rare breed in a sea of games trying to do the same thing -- create an open, honest, vulnerable world that changes with you and remembers your influence. The developers come back week after week, updating and adding to an already enormous map full of seemingly endless tasks. Some complain about the grind in a survival game, while others understand that a certain amount of grind is necessary to feel true reward for your on-screen accomplishments. Icarus finds the perfect balance. 
My only complaint: traveling the map takes way too long. 
If you want 500+ hours worth of playtime, endless updates, tons of optional DLC and a base game that really holds its own, this is your Holy Grail.
